raw_case_text: A 27-year-old male patient with a history of expanding skin lesions was referred to us for further management, after having received a 7-day per os antibiotic treatment with cefuroxime with no improvement. On physical examination there was a nodular, incipiently ulcerated, crumbly lesion 3 x 3 cm in dimension on the extensor surface of the left thigh, as well as crops of multiple elevated dome-shaped nodules and papules of reddish color and shiny, smooth surface on the trunk, the upper and lower extremities, the neck, periorbital and on the genitalia (Figures 1(a) and 1(b)). At some sites there was also a perilesional scaling. No pruritus was mentioned. The palms, the soles, and the mucous membranes were not involved. Moreover, a history of tiredness feeling in the previous months was mentioned. The history revealed though no consistent systemic B symptoms. The differential diagnosis included lymphomatoid papulosis, other cutaneous lymphomas, sarcoidosis, histiocytosis, and cutaneous infections (cutaneous leishmaniasis, atypical mycobacterial infection, and bacillary angiomatosis). Laboratory examination revealed an increased serum title of Bartonella quintana (1/80) and the patient received doxycycline 100 mg 1 x 2 for 2 weeks, with no change in a 2-week control examination. No other abnormal laboratory results were found (serology for CMV, EBV, HIV, HBV, HCV, Toxoplasma, Treponema pallidum, Leishmania, Coxiella burnetii, Mycoplasma pneumonia, Chlamydia pneumonia, Quantiferon test, RF, IgA, IgG, IgM, C3, C4, ANA, and ENA Screen). In the context of a possible histiocytosis we ordered an ophthalmological and an ENT consultation, both of which revealed no pathological signs. We performed two biopsies, one from the ulcerated lesion on the left thigh and another one from a dome-shaped but not ulcerated lesion on the left back. Bacterial, fungal, and mycobacterial cultures from the specimens were negative. Histology revealed a diffuse lymphocytic infiltration in the reticular dermis by small, medium, and large sized lymphocytes, some of which with anaplastic nuclei, accompanied by a variable number of neutrophils and histiocytes (Figures 2(a)-2(c)). Immunophenotypically the lymphocytes were CD3+ (Figure 3(a)), CD30+ (>75%, Figures 3(b) and 3(c)), CD4+, MUM1+, CD8-, ALK-1-, CD15-, and TIA-1-/+ (20% positive). The cellular marker for proliferation, Ki-67, was estimated ~ 80%. The epidermis was spared and showed a psoriasiform hyperplasia. Peripheral blood smear as well as immunophenotypic analysis of peripheral blood and bone marrow was performed with normal findings. The bone marrow biopsy showed absence of neoplastic infiltration, with minor deviations of the hemopoietic series of no particular significance. CT-scan of neck-thorax-abdomen showed no lymphadenopathy. The proposed diagnosis, based upon the correlation of clinical, histological, and immunophenotypical (expression of CD30) findings, was primary cutaneous CD30+ lymphoproliferative disorder with multifocal signs classified as lymphomatoid papulosis type A. According to the NCCN v2.2019 guidelines for primary cutaneous CD30+ T-cell lymphoproliferative disorders for adult patients with extensive disease, observation is preferred for asymptomatic patients. Methotrexate (10 to 35 mg per week by oral or subcutaneous administration) is opted among other treatments in symptomatic patients and has been proposed to our patient due to the large ulcerative lesion on the left thigh and the extensive multifocal disease involving cosmetically important body areas. However, the patient refused to take any medication because of the potential adverse reactions of the therapy. At 4-week follow-up a striking improvement was observed, with the total of the lesions having regressed. Of notice was the regression of the ulcerated nodular lesion on the left thigh (Figures 4(a) and 4(b)). No new lesions were found. A complete response was observed at the follow-up visits, which remained in the last 6 month follow-up.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 27-year-old male presented with a history of expanding multifocal papulonodular skin lesions over his trunk, extremities, neck, periorbital region, and genitalia, including a 3 x 3 cm ulcerated nodule on his left anterior thigh.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed expanding reddish dome-shaped papules and nodules across his body and a larger ulcerated nodule on his left thigh that failed to improve after a 7-day course of oral cefuroxime and a 2-week course of oral doxycycline (100 mg twice daily, given for a 1:80 Bartonella quintana titer), accompanied only by mild fatigue over the preceding months.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for mild fatigue in preceding months; negative for pruritus, fever, night sweats, or weight loss.

objective.physical_examination: A 3 x 3 cm crumbly, incipiently ulcerated nodule on the extensor surface of the left thigh accompanied by crops of reddish, shiny, smooth dome-shaped papules and nodules (some with perilesional scaling) over the trunk, upper and lower extremities, neck, periorbital skin, and genitalia, sparing the palms, soles, and mucous membranes; normal ophthalmological and ENT examinations.
objective.routine_investigations: Peripheral blood smear, RF, IgA, IgG, IgM, C3, C4, ANA, ENA, QuantiFERON-TB, and serologies for Leishmania, CMV, EBV, HIV, HBV, HCV, Toxoplasma, Treponema pallidum, Coxiella burnetii, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, and Chlamydia pneumoniae were all normal or negative (except a borderline 1:80 Bartonella quintana titer).
objective.advanced_workup: Neck, chest, and abdominal CT, peripheral blood and bone marrow immunophenotyping, and bone marrow trephine biopsy showed no systemic lymphoma. Two skin biopsies (left thigh ulcerated nodule and left back dome-shaped nodule) had negative bacterial, fungal, and mycobacterial cultures and demonstrated psoriasiform epidermal hyperplasia overlying a diffuse reticular dermal infiltrate of small, medium, and large anaplastic lymphocytes admixed with neutrophils and histiocytes; immunohistochemistry was positive for CD3, CD30 (>75%), CD4, MUM1, and TIA-1 (20%) with Ki-67 ~80%, and negative for CD8, ALK-1, and CD15.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Cutaneous leishmaniasis, atypical mycobacteriosis, bacillary angiomatosis, sarcoidosis, and histiocytosis were excluded; histopathology and immunohistochemistry (CD3+, CD4+, CD30+ >75%, ALK-1-) confirmed primary cutaneous CD30+ T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder classified as multifocal lymphomatoid papulosis type A. After the patient declined low-dose methotrexate in favor of active observation, all cutaneous lesions—including the ulcerated left thigh tumor—spontaneously regressed within 4 weeks and remained in complete remission at 6-month follow-up.
